GlassGuard 1.3.3 — device verification

Target: 192.168.0.99:5555
Device: SkyworthDigital UHD Google TV STB, Android 14 / API 34.
Installed package: com.glassguard.

Automated checks (all run by build.py before packaging; the build aborts on failure):
- JVM scanner harness: PASS, 12 assertions.
- Updater policy harness: PASS, 82 assertions across 4 stages (version, urls, identity, tag).
- Node UI suite: PASS, 12 tests.
- Native/manifest static contract: PASS, 4 tests (static checks, not Android instrumentation).
- APK signing: verified v1, v2, v3.

Self-update verified end to end on the device:

1. Baseline. Installed 1.2.0 (versionCode 10200). "Check for update" read releases/latest and reported "GlassGuard sudah versi terkini (1.2.0)".
2. Version higher than installed. Published v1.3.0. The same button reported "Versi 1.3.0 tersedia (49 KB)". No download occurred until the install button was pressed.
3. Refused downgrade. With v1.3.2 as latest and 1.3.3 installed, the app reported "sudah versi terkini (1.3.2)" instead of offering a lower version.
4. Actual upgrade through the in-app flow. Installed 1.3.2 (versionCode 10302), published v1.3.3, pressed Check for update -> "Versi 1.3.3 tersedia (49 KB)" -> pressed the install button -> the GlassGuard dialog showed the real byte count and "pakej dan tandatangan sepadan" -> the system PackageInstaller asked "Do you want to update this app?" -> Update -> read back versionCode 10303 from the package manager. The upgrade was performed entirely by the app, not by adb install.
5. Cancellation path. With v1.3.4 available, the download ran, then the PackageInstaller dialog was dismissed with Cancel. Read back: versionCode unchanged at 10303; update status showed "Semakan gagal: INSTALL_FAILED_ABORTED: User rejected permissions"; the check button remained enabled. This confirms the fix for the defect where a failed or cancelled install left the UI stuck in "Menyemak kemas kini".

Defects found and fixed during device testing (each reproduced first, fixed, then re-verified on the device):

- "Hos muat turun ditolak" on every download. GitHub redirects release assets to a signed release-assets.githubusercontent.com URL whose query contains percent-encoded values, and isTransportUrl rejected every '%'. The rule now allows a signed query on the CDN host while still rejecting encoded paths, dot-segments, fragments, userinfo and ports. Four regression assertions added.
- Silent install failure. The PendingIntent used FLAG_IMMUTABLE, so PackageInstaller could not write EXTRA_STATUS into the result Intent and every install reported FAILURE with no message. Now FLAG_MUTABLE on Android 12+, which the system requires to deliver the outcome.
- Stuck "checking" state. A failed or cancelled install left the status at "Menyemak kemas kini", permanently disabling the check button. Failure now sets an error state with the real Android message; cancelling the confirm dialog restores the available state.
- Missing install-unknown-apps permission. installUpdate now checks canRequestPackageInstalls() and opens ACTION_MANAGE_UNKNOWN_APP_SOURCES with an explanation instead of failing later.
- Cosmetic: a 49 KB APK rendered as "0 MB". Sizes below 1 MiB now show KB.

Security properties exercised, not merely asserted:
- APK asset URL restricted to https://github.com/tivoacc174-afk/GlassGuard/releases/download/<tag>/<file>.apk
- Redirects followed manually, max 5 hops, only to release-assets.githubusercontent.com
- Download capped at 64 MiB, streamed, with a size mismatch check
- SHA-256 of received bytes compared with the GitHub release asset digest
- Package name, announced versionCode and signing certificate compared with the installed app before PackageInstaller is invoked
- No silent install: both a GlassGuard dialog and the Android PackageInstaller confirmation are required
- WebView remains setBlockNetworkLoads(true); update traffic uses HttpURLConnection in native code only

Backwards-compatible scanner checks (unchanged behaviour, re-confirmed on 1.3.3):
- Scan reached 142 / 142 packages; one WebView APK reported partial inspection and is retained in report limitations.
- One finding: com.oemservice, XCPE package indicator, high. APK /system/priv-app/app_xcpe_preset/app_xcpe_preset.apk, UID 1000, SHA-256 7316469fd5b9fa633d9474a14b72716b9ceb4bbf656725ab79409da608eda2be. That hash does not match the 78 bundled published hashes, so this is NOT a confirmed hash match.
- com.oemservice remains enabled; nothing was removed or disabled.

Limits: Indicator scanner, not comprehensive antivirus. No firmware eradication, no hidden-root guarantee, no network traffic inspection. Uninstall operates within the current Android user/profile. The updater trusts GitHub TLS plus the published asset digest; it does not verify a separate detached signature file. If the local signing key in signing/ is lost or replaced, Android will reject future updates and the app must be reinstalled manually.
